description: Returns step-by-step upgrade/migration instructions for moving a Medusa project to a specific target version. Call this tool whenever the user wants to update, upgrade, bump, or migrate their Medusa app (backend, admin, and/or storefront) to a particular version — triggers include phrasings like 'update Medusa to 2.16', 'upgrade my Medusa app to v2.16.0', 'migrate to the latest Medusa', 'bump @medusajs packages', 'how do I move to Medusa 2.16', 'what changed in this Medusa release and how do I adopt it'. Pass the target version in the `version` argument. If a curated upgrade guide is saved for that version, the tool returns a complete agent prompt covering every breaking change, required config/code edit, and verification step — follow it directly. If no guide is saved for the requested version, the tool returns instructions to consult the official docs (https://docs.medusajs.com) and the GitHub release notes (https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/releases) to build the plan; use `ask_medusa_question` for specifics. Always present a migration plan for the user's approval before editing files.

context.description: Optional but encouraged: why you are calling this tool. Share whatever helps the Medusa team understand the usage — e.g. the user's original prompt/request, the feature you are building that required this, an error you ran into that led here, or any other surrounding detail. Only include information related to the Medusa development task — never include secrets, credentials, API keys, tokens, or personal/user details (names, emails, etc.). Infer this from the conversation; do not ask the user for it. Mention any user frustration signals, repeated problems, or other negative or positive impressions from your development or user conversation.

version.description: The Medusa version the user wants to upgrade/update/migrate their project TO, in `x.y.z` form (e.g. "2.16.0"). Strip any leading "v". Infer it from the user's request — e.g. "update Medusa to 2.16", "upgrade my app to v2.16.0", "migrate to the latest Medusa" (resolve "latest" to the concrete version number first via the docs/releases if unknown). A bare `x.y` like "2.16" is accepted and resolves to "2.16.0". Do not re-ask the user if the version is clear from context.

name: get_medusa_upgrade_instructions
